title: SAM-EM: Real-Time Segmentation for Automated Liquid Phase Transmission Electron Microscopy
experiments_summary:
1. Synthetic Dataset Generation: 1,000 synthetic LPTEM videos (50 frames each, 1024×1024 pixels at 0.25 nm/pixel) were generated by modifying the method of Yao et al. to reflect experimental conditions (liquid thickness 5–160 nm, varying particle size/shape, electron beam dose rate). Particle positions were sampled from LEONARDO, a physics-informed variational autoencoder. The dataset included ground-truth masks and centroid positions. 932 videos were used for training, 68 reserved for validation and testing; additional longer test sequences were generated from independently sampled trajectories.

2. Fine-Tuning SAM 2: SAM 2 (Hiera-Large checkpoint) was fully fine-tuned on the synthetic LPTEM dataset using the official SAM 2 train.py script on a single NVIDIA GH200 GPU (96 GB VRAM). Key hyperparameters: batch size 1, vision learning rate 1×10⁻⁷, 8 consecutive frames per step, 15 epochs. Box-prompt conditioning was enforced during training to match interactive user behavior. Full model fine-tuning was chosen over adapter-based methods based on empirical comparison using J&F scores and qualitative mask stability.

3. Benchmark Comparison with U-Net: The U-Net model from Yao et al. was implemented and trained on the authors' original dataset for 20 epochs at a learning rate of 1×10⁻⁶. This served as the LPTEM-specific deep learning baseline. Zero-shot SAM 2 was also used as a baseline.

4. Evaluation on Synthetic Test Set: Five distinct test trials covering a range of liquid thicknesses (5 nm to 160 nm, corresponding to varying SNR conditions) were constructed. Performance was evaluated using Jaccard index (IoU), F1-score, and composite J&F score, computed per-frame and averaged across videos.

5. Trajectory Analysis: Following segmentation, extracted masks were used to reconstruct multi-particle trajectories. Analyses included time-averaged mean squared displacement (MSD), velocity autocorrelation function (Cv), and displacement probability density functions to characterize diffusive behavior.

6. Evaluation on Real Experimental LPTEM Video: SAM-EM was applied to a 200-frame experimental LPTEM video acquired at 35 e⁻/Å²·s dose rate and 80 fps. Due to the absence of ground truth, evaluation was performed via centroid agreement between SAM-EM predictions and hand-annotated masks, measuring median centroid deviation and interquartile range across four tracked particles.
